I feel this leads to people putting too much thought into their comments and submissions as they're proud of their score. Users become afraid to post their genuine opinions if they go against the hive mind, which leads to "circlejerk" comments and pandering opinions/observations. Of course comments should still be upvoted/downvoted but a persons karma wouldn't be counted.
We should stop counting user up votes.
I like this idea. Simple, obvious, but no one seems to have thought to say it before.

I think it should display only within a range between -100 and 100 (anything above or below is not shown). You'd be able to tell if someone is not well-liked or if they're able to downvoat, but the limits would discourage both kinds of reputation farming. Those values could be tweaked.

'Voating habits' (up-/downvoats given) should be left as-is though.
Yeah, it's good to know if someone's a troll.
Surely that could be achieved with a cursory glance at previous comments, and seeing the scores for those?

Maybe even instead of a range, you could just have line that says "This user's posts are often ________" and fill that in with things such as "liked", "well received", "disliked", "not well received" etc. That way, there are NO numbers to go along with it, just the general "feeling" or w/e

I like this more than the -100-100 idea. However, personally I think nothing at all is the solution. If you really want to get a picture you can read over past comments.

Overall, does it matter if someone is 'liked' or not? Shouldn't they be treated on the merit of the comment rather than their whole profile?

This is my logic as well. If you really, really need to know a person's history (which again, it shouldn't matter because a single comment is a single comment) why not simply ask? I'm not a fan of making conversation lazy.

well, this kind of thing would only show on their profile, not on each comment. That way, each comment has its own weight/worth as determined by votes, and the profile as a whole if given a weight of some kind as well, that way you can tell at a glance the type of poster that profile belongs to.

do you mean when a user looks at their profile, for all their upvotes? that would work, sweet, actually.

but in comments, do keep the -/+ counter

Yup. This is a slam dunk. At least like moe suggested with the -100 to 100 range so you can test for trolls. Perhaps instead of counting use 3 kinds of badges like Troll(-100), Newbie(0) or Angel(100).
I agree. The whole upvoting/downvoting of comments seems dated. Even for posts I feel there's got to be a better way.
I never thought I wanted this until now. It makes so much sense.

Maybe a "+" or "-" should be put in place of the upvote/downvote count? After maybe 10 upvotes or 10 downvotes it would switch from something neutral (like a "~" symbol) to a more upvoted or more downvoted indicator

I agree with OP, but if the point system is kept, then it should be tied to the comment or submission, not the actual user. That way, circlejerks and low-effort content would be discouraged since at the end of the day you wouldn't be able to jerk off at your total fake internet points count.

If you like quiet laid back slice of life shows, this one's about an android who runs a coffee shop in post-post-apocalyptic rural Japan. It's not violent, so I call it post-post-apocalyptic. The manga has 140 chapters, almost all of which do not really require one to know Japanese. Many chapters have no speech at all. The anime(s) and associated music CDs both have a total of around 90 minutes running time. If you like Columbian/Peruvian Choro music, I'm certain you'll like it. Despite the manga having very little speech, I've found that several readings reveal very subtle things about the world in which Alpha Hasseno/Hatsuseno lives. There's even a small group of enthusiasts who look for the locations shown in YKK, much like other anime. It's the very opposite of Blade Runner.
[Recommendation] Yokohama Kaidashi Kikou / Yokohama Shopping Trip / Quiet Country Cafe
Does the manga cover significantly more content than the anime? I see that it continues for about three years after the anime finished airing.
5 minutes of the anime revolves around roasting beans and preparing coffee in relative silence. The anime is a toe water dipping point with no spoilers to the manga.
